what: Inside the section, 3D coins (a thick rim, a recessed front face and a ring pattern, three.js clearcoat material) pile up with matter-js physics. At first four coins come in one after another at .32s intervals. After that, every 3.2s×(.85~1.15) one coin is thrown in from outside the left in an arc, hits the text box, the floor and other coins, and rolls to rest. When the count passes a set number (computed from section width and height, usually around 10), the oldest coin fades out over .52s and disappears. Dragging a coin makes it follow with a constraint (stiffness .2, damping .12), and releasing it throws it. Coin size is .27 of the band height between floor and text (30~72px), and gravity is set to the section height at 1.9~3.1

options.max: Max number of leaves in the panel, default calculated from panel size (.6x on phones)
options.settle: If on, a set number are pre-stacked from the start (default starts from an empty board)
options.burst: Number of pieces thrown one after another at .32s intervals at the start, default 4
options.fill: Even fill light intensity (instead of the original environment map), default 1.6
options.--fx-coin-1~10: Leaf color list (used in rotation), default six whites/grays plus four accent pinks
options.--fx-shadow: Color of the shadow patch under each leaf, default is the accent color blended slightly into ink black
options.[data-fx-part=floor]: Floor — the top edge of this element is the line where leaves pile up (required)
options.[data-fx-part=solid]: Box where tiles collide and settle (title row, button, etc.). If none, only the floor and walls

note: THREE·Matter are loaded first as globals — matter.min.js goes before three-global.js (the window.exports trick). If placed after, the UMD goes into exports instead of window.Matter and the coins don’t appear. The canvas sits at the very back of the panel (z 0) with text above it — dragging picks up a coin when the press on the whole panel touches one, so buttons over text can still be pressed. The original’s path-finding that hops across letters in turn was reduced to a single thrown parabola: if a letter box is on the incoming side (the 4-coin width at the left), it is thrown from a height above that letter, and while flying it passes behind without colliding with letter boxes, colliding only after it has fully dropped below the text line (this prevents hitting a box corner mid-flight and piling up inside an offscreen wall or resting on the letters). A coin that fails to enter the panel within 2 seconds fades out. If a line box is the full panel width, like a justified line, coins can’t fall between words, so solid is attached per word. It runs only while the panel is on screen and the tab is visible

from.where: index.html hero — original HeroCoins (matter-js 0.20 + three, coins with a carved-in logo)
